report.summary: Chunk 1 of 1: kairos/archive.py defines the Attempt dataclass, digest, load, record, and sample functions for an evolutionary archive.

handoff.purpose: Define the Attempt dataclass and functions for recording, loading, and sampling evolutionary attempts.

symbols.name: OUTCOME_RANK
symbols.note: Dict mapping outcome strings to integer ranks, worst-to-best.

symbols.name: NUM_ELITE
symbols.note: Number of elite attempts to sample (default 3).

symbols.name: NUM_DIVERSE
symbols.note: Number of diverse attempts to sample (default 2).

symbols.name: MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS
symbols.note: Maximum length for the summary field (600 chars).

symbols.name: Attempt
symbols.note: Dataclass representing one evaluated candidate, with fields: attempt_id, outcome, patch_digest, summary, unfixed, ts, meta.

symbols.name: digest_patch
symbols.note: Returns a 16-character hex digest of a patch using SHA-256.

symbols.name: load_attempts
symbols.note: Reads attempts from a JSONL file, returns tuple of Attempts. Skips unparseable lines.

symbols.name: record_attempt
symbols.note: Appends an attempt as a JSON line to the given file. Returns the stored Attempt.

symbols.name: sample_inspirations
symbols.note: Selects elite and diverse attempts from a pool, deduplicating by digest and excluding a given digest.

claims.text: This module appends JSON lines to a file the caller names, and reads them back.
claims.why: record_attempt appends JSON lines; load_attempts reads them.

claims.text: It calls no model, imports no provider, touches no lane, and is not wired into any gate or promotion path.
claims.why: No model or provider imports; no lane or gate references in this code.

claims.text: Every draw here takes an explicit rng, so a run is reproducible and a test can pin the selection instead of retrying until it passes.
claims.why: sample_inspirations has an rng parameter defaulting to random.Random(0).

claims.text: Every field that a candidate can influence is length-capped on the way IN, so a pathological error message cannot grow the file without limit.
claims.why: _truncate caps summary at MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS; unfixed is sliced to 20; patch_digest is fixed-length.

claims.text: This module stores a hash plus a TRUNCATED, caller-supplied summary, and it never reads a candidate's files.
claims.why: Attempt stores patch_digest and truncated summary; no file reading of candidate files.

claims.text: Upstream stores full program source in the archive and pastes it into the next prompt. An archive that holds candidate source is an egress vector... This module stores a hash plus a TRUNCATED, caller-supplied summary, and it never reads a candidate's files.
claims.why: Upstream behavior is not present in this code; claim about upstream is uncheckable.

claims.text: DETERMINISTIC BY DEFAULT. Upstream calls the global random. Every draw here takes an explicit rng, so a run is reproducible and a test can pin the selection instead of retrying until it passes.
claims.why: sample_inspirations uses rng parameter; default is random.Random(0) for determinism.

claims.text: BOUNDED. Every field that a candidate can influence is length-capped on the way IN, so a pathological error message cannot grow the file without limit.
claims.why: summary capped by _truncate; unfixed sliced to 20; patch_digest fixed to 16 chars.

claims.text: NOTHING HERE SPENDS, WRITES CODE, OR GATES ANYTHING
claims.why: No spending, code writing, or gating logic present.

claims.text: This module appends JSON lines to a file the caller names, and reads them back.
claims.why: record_attempt appends; load_attempts reads.

claims.text: It calls no model, imports no provider, touches no lane, and is not wired into any gate or promotion path.
claims.why: No model or provider imports; no lane or gate references.

claims.text: The one safety property worth stating plainly: sample_inspirations returns records, and a record's summary is the ONLY free text on it. A caller that renders these into a prompt is responsible for the egress decision -- this module makes that easy to audit by ensuring there is exactly one field to audit.
claims.why: summary is the only free-text field in Attempt; other fields are structured.

claims.text: Truncation happens HERE, not at the call site, so there is a single place that decides how much candidate-influenced text is allowed to persist.
claims.why: record_attempt calls _truncate on summary before storing.

claims.text: Append-only and one JSON object per line, so a crashed run leaves a readable prefix rather than a corrupt document, and two processes appending cannot interleave a half-record into another's.
claims.why: Uses 'a' mode and writes one JSON line per call.

claims.text: Never raises.
claims.why: Returns empty tuple on missing file or OSError; skips unparseable lines.

claims.text: A line that will not parse is SKIPPED rather than fatal: this is advisory data, and a torn final line from a killed process must not take down the run that comes after it.
claims.why: Uses try-except to skip lines that raise ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError.

claims.text: Adapted from upstream database.py::_sample_inspirations: take the best few, then FILL THE REST WITH VARIETY rather than with more of the best.
claims.why: Upstream code not present; claim about adaptation uncheckable.

claims.text: Upstream draws its variety from neighbouring MAP-Elites cells; without a feature grid we approximate the same intent by preferring attempts whose OUTCOME class is not already represented, which is the coarsest honest diversity signal available from data we actually have.
claims.why: Upstream behavior not present; diversity strategy is implemented in this code.

claims.text: DEDUPLICATION BY DIGEST. Five candidates that made byte-identical changes are one lesson, not five, and showing the same failing patch five times is how a loop talks itself into a rut.
claims.why: Code skips attempts with patch_digest already seen.

claims.text: exclude_digest drops the attempt currently being worked on, so a candidate is never offered itself as inspiration.
claims.why: seen set initialized with exclude_digest; attempts with that digest are skipped.

claims.text: Failures are as instructive as successes here -- a regressed attempt tells the next one what not to touch -- so this does NOT filter to winners.
claims.why: No filtering by outcome; all attempts are considered.

claims.text: Ordering is best-first and fully deterministic given rng.
claims.why: Sorted by rank descending, then ts descending, then attempt_id; rng used only for shuffling diverse pool.

observations.what: record_attempt does not validate that the outcome string is in OUTCOME_RANK; it stores any string.
load_attempts silently skips unparseable lines, which may hide data corruption issues.

sample_inspirations uses rng.shuffle on fresh and stale lists, but the overall order is not fully deterministic if the pool size is large and rng is not provided; default rng=Random(0) provides determinism.
The 'unfixed' field is sliced to 20 in record_attempt but not in Attempt.from_dict, so loading may restore a longer list.
The meta field is not length-capped, potentially allowing unbounded growth.
